reasons: Coverage is broad across policy, storage, display and retrieval, but no test run result was provided.
Stubbed environment values must be cleaned up after each test.

terms.meaning: A written rule file that states what may be done with a data source.
A data source that is only allowed during development, not in the live product.
Turning text into numbers so it can be searched by meaning.
A new piece of data calculated from an original source.

used_by: Run by the test runner as part of the unit tests.

sections.name: File setup, ON, OFF, ACTIONS
sections.title: Setup and action list
sections.what: Imports the rights checker and its error type, the database, the test reset, and fixed settings with prototype data on and off. Lists the six actions that can be checked: store, display, derive, embed, train and video.
sections.why: Gives the rights tests a fixed list of actions to check against each policy.
sections.watch_out: The action list must match the rights checker, or a new action goes untested.

sections.name: rights control plane
sections.title: Rights control plane
sections.what: Checks that every policy file matches the schema and is registered. Checks each action is allowed or denied as the policy says. Checks that Cricsheet may be stored, shown, derived, embedded and trained on but not shown as video. Checks prototype-only sources are blocked when prototype data is off. Checks unknown sources are denied for every action.
sections.why: Likely reason: the policy files define what is allowed, so the checker must read them exactly.
sections.watch_out: A wrong flag in a policy file changes what visitors can see, so policy edits need care.

sections.name: rights enforced by repos and services
sections.title: Enforcement in storage and services
sections.what: Checks that the incident store saves data from licensed sources, skips duplicates, and refuses unlicensed or unknown sources before writing anything. Checks that the live-score route returns a service unavailable status and does not call the outside service when prototype data is off.
sections.why: Likely reason: the rules must be enforced where data is stored and shown, not only written down.
sections.watch_out: Stubbed network and environment values must be removed after the test, or later tests can behave differently.

sections.name: rights enforced by retrieval
sections.title: Enforcement in search
sections.what: Checks that search keeps only documents from sources allowed to be embedded and drops the rest, including unknown sources.
sections.why: Likely reason: search results can reach users, so they must come only from permitted sources.
sections.watch_out: Unknown sources are dropped by default, which is the safe direction for this rule.

sections.name: rights lookups
sections.title: Policy lookup
sections.what: Checks that looking up a source's policy returns it with the Cricsheet credit text, and returns nothing for an unknown source.
sections.why: The credit text is shown to users, so the lookup must return the exact stated wording.
sections.watch_out: Changing the credit text changes what visitors see, so it must be checked against the licence.

summary: Tests the data rights rules: which data sources the app may store, show, derive from, embed, train on, or show video from, and how those rules are enforced in the code paths.
purpose: Makes sure the app only uses data it is permitted to use, and blocks prototype-only sources when prototype data is switched off.
why: Likely reason: using data without permission can break licences, so the app checks the policy before every use.
how: Loads every policy file and checks it matches the schema and is registered. Checks each action is allowed or denied as the policy states. Then checks the enforcement in the database writes, the live-score route and the search retrieval step, and the policy lookup.
inputs: The policy JSON files in the rights policies folder, the rights checker, the database, and the live-score route.
outputs: Pass or fail results, and error messages that name the blocked action or source.
risks: Policy files are the source of truth, so a wrong flag changes what the app may show. Stubbing the network and module state must be undone or later tests can be misled.
debug: Read the error text, which names the source and the action. Check the matching policy file. For the live-score route, check the prototype data setting.
